newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico City volcano belches ash, smoke.
newsitem.headline: Mexico City volcano belches ash, smoke.

text.p: A giant volcano near Mexico City belched ash and smoke 2-1/2 miles (four km) high on Wednesday but officials said there was no immediate danger to the population.

The National Centre for Disaster Prevention (CENAPRED) said in a statement that the eruption of the Popocatepetl volcano was heralded by a minor earth tremor at 10:14 a.m. (1514 GMT) and lasted more than 15 minutes.
"This (tremor) was accompanied by a large exhalation, accompanied by ash which reached an altitude of more than 4 kilometres," the statement said.
Activity at the 17,887-foot (5,465-metre) volcano was moderate but with a tendency to increase, it added.
Winds were likely to blow the ash towards the west and southwest, it said -- an area of small villages and towns. Mexico City is 35 miles (60 km) northwest of the volcano.

Popocatepetl belched ash and smoke periodically in April and May this year, but no major eruptions have occurred since 1720. The government has told people near the volcano to stay alert and watch for warnings but has not ordered any evacuations.
